reflections.title: The God Who Stoops to Lift Us

reflect.text: Praise is more than thanking God for the good things He gives; it is adoring Him simply for who He is. As the Lord of all creation, His majesty sits high above every nation and power. Israel sang this psalm at Passover to celebrate how God delivered them out of slavery, reminding us that the supreme Ruler of the universe never forgets His people.

Although God is enthroned on high, He stoops down to care for the lowly rather than the proud. F. B. Meyer calls this "the psalm of uplifts," pointing out that God is the one who raises the poor and needy from the dust. If you find yourself in a place of influence or comfort, that standing is God's gift to be used for His work, not a reason to boast in yourself.

God reveals His grace most clearly by lifting those who admit their spiritual poverty. Instead of leaving us in the dust, He brings us into fellowship with Himself and seats us in heavenly places with Christ. Believers are given royal access to God's presence, sharing in blessings that outshine all earthly wealth.

questions: In what areas of your life are you tempted to rely on your own strength rather than admitting your need for God?
How does knowing that God lifts the humble change the way you praise Him today?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, You are high above the heavens, yet You look with tender mercy on the poor and needy. Thank You for lifting us out of our spiritual emptiness and welcoming us into fellowship with You through Christ. Help us to walk humbly before You and to use every gift You provide for Your glory. Amen.
